harm_summary: Directs a mass audience at a named child; standard harassment pipeline
who_benefited: Culture-war engagement + ad pivot in the same segment
society_effect: CAREFUL: the child is a victim, not a figure to debate. No name, no clips, no images in any FoF cut. We deliberately did not create an entity row for the minor.

short_title: Send veterans and bikers to watch city precincts
claim_summary: Around the 2016 election, on Coach Dave's show, Larry Nichols urges 'veterans' and 'biker gangs' to stake out inner-city polling places to stop fraud he cannot document, and blames Soros. Revisited on KF #241.
harm_summary: Openly advocates voter intimidation aimed at Black neighborhoods; federal law forbids it
who_benefited: Grifter cross-promotion between two small shows
society_effect: 2016 version of the poll-watcher push that scales up in 2020

short_title: Corporate PR read as anti-globalist news
claim_summary: April 2009: Jones reads Rick Berman's Center for Consumer Freedom material on air as independent reporting (getting the group's name wrong), making an industry front group's copy into grassroots truth.
harm_summary: Audience receives paid industry messaging as resistance journalism
who_benefited: The front group got free distribution; the show got free copy
society_effect: Answers the charter question directly: who paid for what he read? Need CCF funding filings.

short_title: Immigrants are wolves eating the sheep
claim_summary: April 2009: immigrants described as wolves who came to eat us, with callers egged on and slurs defended on air. Recurs in 2018 as the caravan invasion package.
harm_summary: Dehumanization of a whole population; feeds later caravan panic
society_effect: Same machine as #225. Document the pattern; do not replay the slurs as content.

short_title: Soros runs the media and will start a civil war
claim_summary: April 8 2009 — the day Soros becomes the villain. Jones says Soros runs Media Matters, owns Air America, is hated by The Obama Deception, will start a civil war, is wanted for arrest by many nations, and is behind the demonization of right-wing militias. KF marks this episode as the start of the Soros narrative.
harm_summary: Launches the antisemitic scapegoat that carries the next fifteen years of programming
who_benefited: A single name to blame for everything, endlessly reusable
society_effect: Datable origin point. Soros had not funded Media Matters in April 2009 — his first donation was $1M in October 2010, and he said so publicly. Air America had been owned by the Green brothers since 2007.

claim_summary: Jones's founding credential: that his July 25 2001 broadcast predicted the September 11 attacks. On the tape he mentions Bin Laden, and separately mentions the World Trade Center and explosions, never joined into a prediction. Bill Cooper said close to the same thing on June 28 2001, and was somewhat more specific.
harm_summary: The prophecy credential that made everything after it sound authoritative
society_effect: Cooper got there first, and Jones repaid him by trashing him and inventing a story about him cursing on air. Need the original July 25 2001 and June 28 2001 recordings.

short_title: The 9/11 hackers are good guys in the government
claim_summary: January 2019 — a crew calling itself thedarkoverlord steals 9/11 litigation files from insurers and demands bitcoin. Jones teases the leak as the story that will break everything, uses Q language around it, and says the hackers are patriots inside the government. They told Forbes plainly they were doing it to fuel their bitcoin wallets.
harm_summary: Promotes an active criminal extortion campaign to a mass audience; Nathan Wyatt got five years and about $1.5M restitution
who_benefited: The extortionists got free publicity; the show got a cliffhanger
society_effect: Cleanest example of the pattern: anyone claiming to have secret documents is automatically a patriot, and the paperwork later says criminal.

short_title: We are already under martial law, so Trump should seize power
claim_summary: January 8 2019 — Mike Adams argues on air that Obama already installed martial-law powers (pointing at EO 13603) to hand to Hillary, that the country is technically under martial law now, and that Trump should therefore seize the power, bypass posse comitatus and declare war on his opponents. Jones agrees and says he wants it.
harm_summary: Open advocacy for a coup by executive order, aimed at an audience already primed for it
who_benefited: Adams's supplement brand; the show's wall-crisis coverage
society_effect: EO 13603 is a Defense Production Act delegation about industrial preparedness. Read the text next to the claim. This is the same camp-myth machinery pointed at a president they like.

short_title: Nobody has ever declared a national emergency
claim_summary: January 2019 — while arguing Trump should declare a national emergency for the wall, Jones claims no one has ever done it except Reagan with the air traffic controllers.
harm_summary: Makes routine statutory authority sound like a historic seizure of power
who_benefited: Drama; the sense of a decisive moment arriving
society_effect: Dozens of national emergencies declared under the 1976 National Emergencies Act were active at the time. Easy on-screen kill with the Federal Register list.

short_title: We use the Tea Party to radicalize people
claim_summary: April 8 2009, on air, in the middle of the Oath Keepers segment: Jones describes using the Tea Party to radicalize people, and says he wants to use the Oath Keepers as 'the final solution'. Not a claim to debunk — a description of the plan in his own words.
harm_summary: States recruitment intent plainly, one day after defending the Pittsburgh shooter
who_benefited: Movement growth; the Oath Keepers got a national platform
society_effect: The single most quotable line of the 2009 investigation. CAREFUL: 'final solution' is his phrase — present it as evidence, with the Holocaust echo named, not as a gotcha.

claim_summary: January 15 2019 — Jones runs cover for Rep. Steve King after his white-supremacy remarks, recycles immigrant crime statistics, launches caravan panic season two, and claims China owns most US movie studios and is forcing Americans to be gay.
harm_summary: Mainstreams open white nationalism by treating it as free-speech martyrdom
who_benefited: King's standing with the base; the show's culture-war lane
society_effect: CAREFUL: document the defense, do not restate the rhetoric as content. The China / movie-studio line is a check-and-kill with actual ownership records.

claim_summary: January 2019 — covering the Lincoln Memorial confrontation, Jones defends the Covington students, praises MAGA spaces, and describes Nathan Phillips, the Omaha elder in the video, as looking like a demonic snake.
harm_summary: Dehumanizing language aimed at a named private individual mid-news-cycle
society_effect: CAREFUL: a genuinely contested news event where early reporting was wrong in places. Our subject is the dehumanization, not relitigating the encounter.

short_title: Fake intel doctor, remote poisoning, and ZOG
claim_summary: April 2016 Project Camelot interview: a naturopath using a false name claims an intelligence background, militia command, that space vibrations rewrite DNA, that a coronal mass ejection made him ill, and that he is being poisoned remotely. He pushes gold through UPMA and predicts a summer of rage after the 2016 RNC. His site runs ZOG antisemitism and Cassidy lets the message air.
harm_summary: Medical misinformation plus antisemitic conspiracy, sold alongside gold referrals
who_benefited: UPMA gold sales; his own consulting brand
society_effect: Keep it because Jones repeats these exact talking points on #251 three days later, including the three-senator Fed story from #242. Shows the fringe-to-Alex pipeline running in days. CAREFUL: skip-tier for video; no ZOG material on screen.

short_title: War-crime advocacy over the piracy crisis
claim_summary: April 2009 — during the Maersk Alabama period Jones riffs admiringly about Somali pirates, then advocates actions against them that amount to war crimes, alongside claims about secret public testing.
harm_summary: Normalizes atrocity talk on a mass-market show
society_effect: CAREFUL: document the rhetoric, never repeat it, no ethnic framing. Pairs with the authoritarian-admiration thread that peaks on #251.

claim_summary: April 2009 — Jones announces he is shooting a chemtrail documentary and books activist Rosalind Peterson as the expert, treating persistent contrails as a deliberate spraying program.
harm_summary: Long-running distrust of atmospheric science; harassment of researchers
who_benefited: Another film to sell, in the Endgame / Obama Deception factory pattern
society_effect: Third documentary of the year built the same way: pick a fear, book a credentialed-sounding guest, shoot B-roll, sell the DVD.

short_title: Trying to co-opt Occupy Wall Street
claim_summary: September 25 2011, the day after roughly 80 peaceful Occupy protesters were arrested in New York: Jones spends the show trying to fold Occupy into his own movement rather than covering the arrests, while staying on board with the Tea Party and Ron Paul.
harm_summary: Real protest suppression goes uncovered in favor of movement recruitment
who_benefited: Audience growth from a left-coded moment
society_effect: Useful contrast: he claims to oppose the banks, but the actual anti-bank movement is only interesting as a recruiting pool. Get the NYPD arrest figures.

claim_summary: Jan 25 2019: after FBI arrests Roger Stone on a seven-count Mueller indictment (false statements, obstruction, witness tampering), Jones treats it as a frame-up aimed at InfoWars, worries he is next because of Corsi, and hosts Stone's lawyer. Stone's own press conference line: 'I am falsely accused of making false statements.'
harm_summary: Converts a charging document about lying to Congress into persecution theater; jury later convicted on all seven counts (Nov 15 2019)
who_benefited: Stone's martyr brand; InfoWars victim narrative
society_effect: Primary is the indictment itself (D.D.C. 1:19-cr-00018). Pair with the Nov 2019 verdict. Seed for a later Stone deep-dive — he is the Trump-flip architect AND a documented liar under oath.

short_title: Loyalty flip: dump Stone when he costs money
claim_summary: Within days of the indictment (#259) Jones says he is tired of Roger, cannot afford him, and wants to cover more than Trump. By #264 the line is 'Fuck you Roger Stone!' Same loyalty pattern as the Face Turn walkback: useful until expensive.
harm_summary: Shows the network is transactional, not principled
who_benefited: Jones distance from a newly radioactive ally
society_effect: Teaching beat for the Stone deep-dive: the man who flipped InfoWars to Trump gets discarded the week the paperwork arrives. Not a falsity claim — a character receipt.

short_title: Sandy Hook day-of: gut says staged
claim_summary: Dec 14 2012, the day of the shooting: after gun talk and a Big Jim Tucker Turkey distraction, Jones floats that it may be staged, says his gut says staged, asks a Weather Underground guest if it was fake, and closes on 'real or not? who knows!' while tying the dead children to globalists.
harm_summary: Same-day seeding of the denial that later produced Texas court findings and family harassment
who_benefited: Gun-rights fear content; later crisis-actor lore
society_effect: CAREFUL — courts/docs/mechanism only. No victim names, no cruelty montage. This is episode one of KF's Sandy Hook investigation: how fast the 'staged' frame arrived.

short_title: American Free Press hate guest on air
claim_summary: April 14 2009: Big Jim Tucker of Willis Carto's American Free Press uses the n-word about Clarence Thomas on InfoWars; Alex tries to spin it. Same hour books Argentine antisemite Adrian Salbuchi. Hate-press DNA sitting in the Tea Party guest book.
harm_summary: Open racial slur and antisemitic guest hour on a mass show
who_benefited: AFP / Carto pipeline gets national distribution
society_effect: Hate-guest standards beat, same lane as Manning/Anderson. Document network; do not replay the slur or Salbuchi's material.

short_title: Tea Party mystery solved: he cannot read the documents
claim_summary: April 12-13 2009: KF's verdict that the Tea Party investigation is essentially over — Alex introduces at least two completely misrepresented documents, admits it does not matter what the report says, and claims Tea Party ownership while bullying into stories. Naomi Wolf is the guest while he fails basic document literacy.
harm_summary: Method exposed: fear first, paperwork optional
society_effect: Pairs with #246 FEMA evidence collapse. Method video: put the actual reports on screen.

short_title: Bell Curve / racial IQ on air
claim_summary: Feb 2019: Alex cites Charles Murray's The Bell Curve, racial IQ claims, and 'cold weather makes people smart' framing during a bigotry hour that also targets Ilhan Omar and recycles Democrat-blackface panic.
harm_summary: Scientific racism laundered as forbidden knowledge
society_effect: CAREFUL: document that the show platformed the claim; do not restage racial-IQ debate. Same hour: 'Fuck you Roger Stone!' — loyalty dump continues.

short_title: Rogan feud as persecution / money crisis
claim_summary: Feb 2019: Alex frames a Joe Rogan dispute as victimization, threatens to 'slit Joe's throat... politically,' brings Mike Adams on to pile on, cites Stubblebine on interdimensional aliens, and ends on InfoWars needing money badly.
harm_summary: Rival-platform fight sold as existential martyrdom while cash is short
society_effect: Character tape post-ban: money hole + enemy inflation.

short_title: Beat kids / teachers should hit students
claim_summary: Sept 1 2011: roughly a third of the show arguing teachers should hit students, raising kids is like training a dog, football coaches should be allowed to break jaws, and common law lets you beat your kids — same hour Ron Paul agrees on FEMA camps.
harm_summary: Normalizes child abuse as parenting / education policy
society_effect: Character/values tape more than a falsifiable claim. Low video priority.

claim_summary: KF #263 (Jordan-hosted, not an Alex day): Marc Morano / CFACT ClimateDepot method — cherry-picked sea-level and ice stats, fossil-fuel-adjacent funding, science-as-enemy framing.
harm_summary: Public distrust of climate science for industry-adjacent messaging
society_effect: Peripheral to InfoWars core. Seed for a later FoF climate short if David wants one. Need CFACT funding docs before scripting.

short_title: Sandy Hook: fourteen days from gun politics to false flag
claim_summary: Traced day by day across #267-#275: on Dec 16 it is a gun-grab story with 'I smell something rotten'; on Dec 17-18 he calls the shooting a 'simulation' and says his gut says government involvement; on Dec 19 he pushes a second shooter and turns the corner; on Dec 20 the official story is 'a fable'; by Dec 23-31 he says false flag outright.
harm_summary: The narrative that produced a decade of harassment of bereaved families and, eventually, the Texas and Connecticut defamation judgments
who_benefited: Alex Jones; gun and preparedness advertisers; the false-flag brand
society_effect: Made denial of a mass killing of children into a mainstream conspiracy position

short_title: Second shooter fled into the woods
claim_summary: Dec 19 2012 onward: a second shooter was caught or fled at Sandy Hook, proving a coordinated operation rather than a lone killer.
harm_summary: First load-bearing factual claim in the denial structure; everything later is built on it
society_effect: Turned the confusion of a breaking news morning into permanent evidence of conspiracy

short_title: The shooter had no rifle, only handguns
claim_summary: Dec 20 2012: Alex tells the audience the shooter carried only two handguns and no Bushmaster, so the assault-weapons response is built on a lie.
harm_summary: A checkable falsehood repeated for years; useful precisely because it can be closed in one page of the official report
who_benefited: Alex Jones; opponents of the assault-weapons bill
society_effect: Model of how a specific wrong fact keeps a general doubt alive

claim_summary: Dec 19 2012: within five days Alex starts criticising the bereaved parents for how they grieve and speak in public. The earliest documented beat of the conduct that the defamation cases would later be about.
harm_summary: Years of harassment, threats and relocation for Sandy Hook families; later Texas and Connecticut judgments
society_effect: Normalised treating grieving families as adversaries in a media fight

short_title: Sandy Hook was a false flag against Alex
claim_summary: Feb 2019 on JRE #1255: because the media said he called Sandy Hook a false flag, people concluded it was a false flag aimed at him, which he offers as reason to think Sandy Hook really was a false flag. The premise is his own earlier lie, recycled as evidence.
harm_summary: Restated denial to a mass audience while the families' suits were live
society_effect: Perfect closed loop: the coverage of a lie becomes the proof of the lie

short_title: The field manual that proves false flags
claim_summary: Dec 17-18 2012: Alex points at Operation Gladio and at Supplement B to US Army Field Manual 30-31, the 'strategy of tension' document, as proof that Western governments order attacks on their own civilians and blame the left.
harm_summary: The general licence under which specific atrocities get called staged
who_benefited: Soviet active-measures programmes first, conspiracy media ever since
society_effect: A KGB forgery became a permanent fixture of American anti-government belief

short_title: The UN treaty will take your guns
claim_summary: Dec 2012: the UN Arms Trade Treaty is presented as the instrument that will disarm Americans, quoted selectively on air.
harm_summary: Confiscation panic; drove buying and militia recruitment after a massacre
who_benefited: Gun retailers and advertisers; the NRA's post-Sandy Hook counter-offensive
society_effect: A trade-paperwork treaty became a decade-long fear engine

short_title: The Pentagon built shooter games to condition killers
claim_summary: Dec 2012: shoot-em-ups were designed by the Defense Department to make people willing to kill, so ban games and antidepressants before touching guns.
harm_summary: Redirects a policy argument onto a cause the evidence does not support
society_effect: The true kernel (the Army did fund a recruiting shooter) is used to carry an unsupported conclusion

short_title: China demands Americans be disarmed, and we broke it
claim_summary: Dec 20 2012: China is calling for the disarmament of American citizens; Alex says InfoWars broke the story. It came from Breitbart, off Chinese state-media opinion writing, and Pravda then credited InfoWars, which was treated as confirmation.
harm_summary: Foreign-threat framing bolted onto domestic gun politics
who_benefited: Alex Jones' reputation as a breaker of stories
society_effect: Cleanest available specimen of circular sourcing: the echo is mistaken for a second witness

short_title: The psychiatry expert who is not one
claim_summary: Dec 2012: Kelly O'Meara is presented as an investigative authority on psychiatric drugs and shootings. She holds no psychology or medical qualification, wrote for CCHR (founded by the Church of Scientology) and for Insight, a Unification-Church-owned magazine.
harm_summary: Gives a church campaign the appearance of independent research at the exact moment gun policy is being decided
who_benefited: CCHR and the wider anti-psychiatry campaign; Alex's need for credentialed-sounding guests
society_effect: Shows how an expert is manufactured: movement outlet, then book, then radio, then 'author and investigator'

short_title: AOC is a front for Soros money
claim_summary: March 2019: Alex announces he has figured out that Ocasio-Cortez is a front for Soros funding, alongside on-air mockery of her appearance.
harm_summary: Antisemitic scapegoating template attached to a new target; sustained threat environment for both named people
who_benefited: Alex Jones; the wider Soros-puppet industry
society_effect: The bogeyman machine demonstrably reusable on whoever is newly prominent

short_title: Summers wants to ship toxic waste to Brazil
claim_summary: Jan 2013: Alex says Larry Summers wants to dump toxic waste on Brazil. The underlying 1991 World Bank memo, drafted by Lant Pritchett and signed by Summers, argued that polluting industry tends to migrate to lower-income countries. Real document, ugly argument, not Alex's version of it.
harm_summary: Discredits legitimate criticism by overstating it
society_effect: Good teaching case: the true version is damning enough, and the exaggeration is what makes it dismissable

short_title: Calling Oklahoma City a globalist plot gives the movement cover
claim_summary: Jan 2013: the OKC-as-inside-job story, and Dan's argument for why it persists -- it lets the patriot movement disown the deadliest thing it produced, and gives it an exit whenever heat arrives.
harm_summary: Erases responsibility for 168 deaths and the movement's own role in radicalising the bomber
who_benefited: Militia and patriot media needing distance from McVeigh
society_effect: A movement that cannot own its worst outcome cannot be corrected by it

short_title: The toy store that ran guns
claim_summary: Jan 2013: guest Bob Fletcher says his toy company was bought by Gary Best and used to move weapons for Iran-Contra, and that he helped start the patriot militia movement.
harm_summary: None direct; an unchecked resume presented as insider testimony
who_benefited: Fletcher's standing as a witness; Alex's supply of insiders
society_effect: Shows the format's core failure -- nobody ever asks for the paperwork

claim_summary: Jan 2013: serial killers and mass shooters are explained as satanists, a straight continuation of 1980s satanic panic inside a gun-policy argument.
harm_summary: Replaces any usable account of violence with a supernatural one
society_effect: Satanic panic never ended, it was absorbed

short_title: Christchurch was a false flag / synthetic attack
claim_summary: March 15 2019, hours after the Christchurch mosque massacres: Jones floats Ides-of-March false-flag lore, plays a blurred livestream clip, calls the attack synthetic, and uses the manifesto to claim the right is being framed while pivoting into Muslim-blame and guest justification. The manifesto title is The Great Replacement — the same demographic panic the show had been selling for years.
harm_summary: Same-day denial and victim-blame after 51 worshippers murdered; normalises the ideology named in the manifesto while stripping empathy from Muslim dead
who_benefited: InfoWars fear content; white-nationalist narrative industry
society_effect: Teaches the audience that even livestreamed white-terrorist massacres are suspect if they threaten the brand

short_title: Sandy Hook denial was 'psychosis'; still something fishy
claim_summary: March 14 2019 videotaped deposition in Lewis v. Jones: Jones claims a past 'form of psychosis' made him think everything was staged, still suggests something fishy, cannot identify the date of the shooting, admits Wolfgang Halbig and 4chan as major sources, and is confronted with outing Leonard Pozner / HONR and the Lucy Richards threats case. Lawyers object constantly; he still frames himself as the victim.
harm_summary: Under-oath continuation of the denial that produced family harassment and later Texas/Connecticut judgments; psychosis line tries to erase intent
who_benefited: Legal defense narrative; InfoWars brand management
society_effect: Shows the product does not stop when the courts arrive — it renames itself

claim_summary: January 4–6 2013, three weeks after the shooting: Jones says Sandy Hook is scripted, books militia-theater police chief Mark Kessler on 'gun heaven' and secession, and keeps the gun-grab cycle running while RT coverage of him becomes a grievance. Extends the Chunk 3 fortnight ladder into January.
harm_summary: Keeps denial live into the new year while recruiting militia energy
who_benefited: Alex Jones; gun and preparedness advertisers; militia guests
society_effect: Shows the ladder did not stop at 'false flag' — it hardened into script language

short_title: Alex goes public courting the QAnon crowd
claim_summary: April 5 2019: after a caller brings up Q, Jones is openly down with Q, flashbacks to already knowing Q's info, tries to position himself as the storm, and pushes Zack-from-Space-Command as a house brand alternative. The overture sits inside an hour of anti-LGBT hunting rhetoric with MassResistance.
harm_summary: Pulls Q audience onto InfoWars while amplifying eliminationist talk about drag performers
who_benefited: InfoWars audience capture; MassResistance; Q-adjacent monetizers
society_effect: Marks the shift from absorbing Q language (#247–#250) to publicly courting the crowd

short_title: Molyneux Poland film as nationalist tourism
claim_summary: December 2018 mini-doc '100 Year March: A Philosopher in Poland': Stefan Molyneux (no philosophy degree) soft-launders Polish far-right politics, misses curated think-tank staging (Warsaw Enterprise Institute / Freedom Lounge), and sells national-pride nostalgia to a US white-nationalist audience. KF #285 is the deep dive.
harm_summary: Exports far-right nationalist aesthetics as 'philosophy' to US viewers
who_benefited: Molyneux brand; Polish nationalist hosts; Free Domain Radio
society_effect: Same demographic-panic industry as Christchurch-week content, sold as travel doc

claim_summary: April 4 2019: Dan maps Alex's standing myths (racial memory, demon-looking overlords, chemicals changing children, fight the overlords / follow Jesus) onto Arthur C. Clarke's Childhood's End. Method claim: a sci-fi novel is doing structural work that the audience hears as news analysis.
harm_summary: Low direct harm; useful literacy beat about fiction recycled as prophecy
society_effect: Teaching tool for how unfalsifiable lore stays sticky

short_title: Crisis actors: InfoWars origin dated Jan 2013
claim_summary: January 7–9 2013, days after the Piers Morgan appearance: Alex starts the actor/coaching narrative on air, credits gut that is 'never wrong,' and the pipeline traces to FAU professor James Tracy. Colorado and Sandy Hook are both 'staged'; more will be staged. This is the dated origin of the crisis-actor product later recycled at Parkland and beyond — earlier than the 2015 Hamamoto lane.
harm_summary: Template for years of family harassment; Tracy later demanded Pozners prove their murdered child existed; Texas/CT judgments follow the same conduct
who_benefited: Alex Jones; denial-industry bloggers; Tracy's brand
society_effect: Turned bereaved parents into suspected performers — the core of the later suits

short_title: Defends Christchurch shooter's motivation / ethnic cleansing talk
claim_summary: April 25–26 2019, six weeks after Christchurch: Alex says 'damn right I'm Islamophobic,' defends the shooter's motivation, and drifts into breeding-program / ethnic-cleansing talk while retreading Charlottesville as a six-part false flag. Same arc as the day-after false-flag hour (#277) — now without the soft-pedal.
harm_summary: Normalises white-terrorist motive after 51 dead; escalates demographic panic into eliminationist language
who_benefited: InfoWars fear brand; white-nationalist narrative industry
society_effect: Shows the Great Replacement product after the massacre: not remorse — defense

short_title: May 2019 Facebook/Instagram ban = proof of truth
claim_summary: May 2 2019 Facebook permanently bans Alex Jones, InfoWars, Paul Joseph Watson, Laura Loomer and others under dangerous-individuals policy (with Instagram). On air (#293) Alex spins it as anti-semitism framing, Jesus comparison, head-for-the-hills, sue-everyone-but-needs-money — classic A-DEPLATFORM martyr + sales move, second wave after Aug 2018.
harm_summary: Converts TOS enforcement into persecution proof and donation ask
who_benefited: InfoWars sales; Loomer guest hour for mutual martyrdom
society_effect: Second-wave deplatforming still teaches 'banned = true'

short_title: Notre Dame fire = fall of West / Islam / Soros
claim_summary: April 2019 Notre Dame fire coverage: represents the fall of the West, will become a mosque, pushed toward arson/Christian-persecution narrative via PI News blog numbers, then blamed on ISIS and Soros. Does not call it a false flag — but launders it into the same demographic-panic machine as Christchurch week.
harm_summary: Weaponises a cathedral fire into anti-Muslim demographic panic
who_benefited: InfoWars fear content; PI News / Islamophobic blog pipeline
society_effect: Same week as Christchurch aftermath content — continuous panic product

claim_summary: January 15–16 2013, a month after Sandy Hook: on air a caller will send Obama a copy of John Ross's Unintended Consequences; Alex engages the recommendation. McVeigh later said if Turner Diaries was his Bible, Unintended Consequences was his New Testament — and that reading it earlier might have pushed him toward sniper attrition instead of a truck bomb.
harm_summary: Normalises a novel McVeigh endorsed as operationally preferable, one month after a school massacre
society_effect: Shows the post-SH reading list: not comfort — attrition fantasy

claim_summary: January 15–16 2013: Alex says Adam Lanza is a patsy — another rung on the denial ladder after simulation / fable / false flag / scripted / crisis actors.
harm_summary: Keeps multi-actor conspiracy alive against the sole-shooter finding
society_effect: Pairs with second-shooter claim; official report closes both

short_title: Sandy Hook lawyer planted child porn to frame Jones
claim_summary: June 14 2019: after InfoWars produced discovery files containing embedded child-porn images, Jones names plaintiffs' lawyer Chris Mattei on air, pounds his photo, accuses him of planting the files, and offers a $1 million reward. Judge Bellis finds he was accusing counsel, calls the broadcast indefensible, and sanctions him (no special motions to dismiss; fees).
harm_summary: On-air targeting of opposing counsel in an active family lawsuit; court called it possibly criminal; families' lawyers had already referred the images to the FBI
society_effect: Turns a discovery failure into a frame-up story and a threat broadcast. Courts/docs only; do not replay the images or the rant.

short_title: Congo Ebola immigrants are a bioweapon at the US border

claim_summary: 1997-1999: the date bug cannot be fixed in time, so power, water, banking, food distribution and government will fail at once and modern society will collapse. Gary North predicted every Western government would be destroyed and, per Thomas Ice, 1.5 billion deaths. Ed Yourdon's Time Bomb 2000 made the cascading-failure argument respectable. Michael Hyatt called anything less than major disruption 'downright impossible in my view.' Floor: the Senate Special Committee's Feb 2000 final report, 'Y2K Aftermath -- Crisis Averted' -- hundreds of minor problems, none causing serious disruption.
harm_summary: Followers cashed out retirement accounts and paid tax penalties, took on debt, relocated to rural retreats, and were left with the bills and public humiliation. One documented case spent more than $50,000 over 18 months; another walked away from a mortgage and career. A couple who relocated publicly later divorced.
who_benefited: Book publishers and authors; preparedness and food sellers; gold dealers; broadcasters who held audiences with countdown programming
society_effect: Established the modern template: take a real technical problem, declare it unfixable, sell the escape kit. Every later crisis-plus-product cycle runs this play.

short_title: Collapse is the point: 'Y2K is our deliverance'
claim_summary: Gary North, writing to fellow Christian Reconstructionists on his own site: 'The Y2K crisis is systemic. It cannot possibly be fixed. I think it will wipe out every national government in the West. Not just modify them -- destroy them... That is what I have wanted all my adult life. In my view, Y2K is our deliverance. Just don't be in a city when deliverance occurs.' The motive is not inferred, it is stated. He wanted the collapse because Reconstructionist theology needs the secular state gone before biblical law can be rebuilt.
harm_summary: Followers who took his advice to leave the cities acted on a prediction its own author wanted to come true. The most severe documented personal losses cluster in this retreat-and-stockpile lane.
who_benefited: North's site traffic, newsletter and movement authority; the Reconstructionist project generally
society_effect: The clearest documented case in the whole database of a forecaster wanting his own catastrophe. Teaching beat: check whether the person predicting the disaster would enjoy it.

short_title: Y2K is God's instrument / a chance for revival
claim_summary: 1998-1999: religious broadcasters reframed a software date problem as divine judgment or an opportunity for national revival. Jerry Falwell's $28 videotape 'A Christian's Guide to the Millennium Bug' said Y2K may 'be God's instrument to humble this nation,' asked 'Could this be God's way to bring revival to America?', compared the Tower of Babel to 'the Y2K computer crisis of long ago,' and told viewers that when nothing is available 'the people who have those things will be in mortal danger of attack from those who don't have them.' Pat Robertson ran 700 Club segments titled 'A Date with Disaster' and 'Countdown to Chaos.'
harm_summary: Congregations were told by trusted pastors to prepare for civil breakdown. Hank Hanegraaff warned at the time that people who made life decisions on these predictions would leave the church afterward. Dobson and Hyatt later apologized.
who_benefited: Video and book sales; broadcast audience retention; the Christian retail category, which trade press called the hottest-selling around
society_effect: Moved apocalypse marketing from the fringe into mainstream pulpits, and spent congregational trust on a prediction that failed within a single night.

short_title: Buy the year of food, the tape, the gold
claim_summary: 1998-1999: the fear resolved into a shopping list. Michael Hyatt's Y2K Prep sold a one-year four-person food package for $3,395 plus shipping and urged customers to buy the top tier even if they thought the bug would be minor, so they would not have to 'turn friends and neighbors into adversaries.' Falwell sold a $28 tape. Van Impe sold '2000 Time Bomb.' Consolidated Marketing sold an $89 survival kit containing an abacus. On the Alex Jones broadcast of Dec 31 1999 the fear ran alongside survival food and Midas Resources gold ads in the same hour.
harm_summary: Documented individual losses from tens of thousands of dollars up to six figures, plus IRA liquidation penalties, abandoned mortgages and careers, and lasting debt after the goods proved unnecessary.
who_benefited: Hyatt and Y2K Prep; Thomas Nelson and Christian retail; Falwell and Van Impe video sales; gold dealers including Midas Resources and Ted Anderson; generator and gun sellers
society_effect: Basic preparedness is sensible; that is what makes this work. The sale was the scale and the deadline. Same wrapper used later for supplements, gold and survival food across the whole InfoWars era.

short_title: Y2K triggers UN takeover and martial law
claim_summary: 1999: militia and antigovernment figures taught that Y2K computer failures would collapse American infrastructure and give the United Nations the opening to seize the country, with martial law declared first. Norm Olson of the Northern Michigan Regional Militia predicted constitutional rights would be suspended before the crisis hit and called it 'the worst time for humanity since the Noahic flood.' Some held that power would be shut off deliberately to manufacture the excuse. The FBI documented the whole lane in Project Megiddo (Oct 20 1999). On Dec 31 1999 Alex Jones ran the same product: Austin camps, Arkansas martial-law signs, military trains.
harm_summary: No takeover, no camps, no martial law. Project Megiddo records extremists acquiring weapons and surveying targets in anticipation. The FBI report itself was then folded back in as proof of the coming crackdown.
who_benefited: Militia recruitment during a fear peak; broadcasters selling the martial-law lane, Jones among them
society_effect: Direct ancestor of the FEMA camp arc and every later 'they will use this crisis to declare martial law' cycle, through 9/11, Ebola, COVID and beyond. The 1999 version is the cleanest to teach because the deadline came and went on camera.

short_title: The banks will fail: get your money out
claim_summary: 1999: predictions that banking would fail at the date change, with calls to withdraw savings, buy gold, and hold cash. Ranged from mainstream anxiety to James Wickstrom's Christian Identity version, which claimed banks, registers, pensions and deliveries would all stop and that Jewish bankers were concealing the danger to prevent a run. Documented in the ADL's Y2K report and the FBI's Project Megiddo. Floor: the Federal Reserve put an extra $50 billion into circulation as a precaution, and no banking collapse occurred.
harm_summary: Savers took tax penalties to liquidate retirement accounts. Gold buyers bought at a fear premium into a market that did not move as promised.
who_benefited: Gold and precious-metals dealers, including the Midas Resources lane advertising on the same broadcasts; extremist recruiters using the collapse frame
society_effect: CAREFUL -- the extremist variant is explicitly antisemitic. Document the mechanism only: an old blood-libel-adjacent banking conspiracy attached itself to a routine software problem. Never quote or restage the antisemitic content.
